lines: Title: The automorphism group of the doubly-even [72,36,16] code can only be of order 1, 3 or 5
\title{The automorphism group of the doubly-even $[72,36,16]$ code can only be   of order $1$, $3$ or $5$}

We prove that a putative $[72,36,16]$ code is not the image of linear code over $\ZZ_4$, $\FF_2 + u \FF_2$ or $\FF_2+v\FF_2$, thus proving that the extremal doubly-even $[72,36,16]$ binary code cannot have an automorphism group containing a fixed point free involution. Combining this with the previously proved result by Bouyuklieva that such a code cannot have an automorphism group containing an involution with fixed points, we conclude that the automorphism group of the $[72,36,16]$ code cannot be of even order, leaving $1$, $3$ and $5$ as the only possibilities.

A long standing open problem asks whether a binary $[72,36,16]$ Type~II code exists, where Type~II indicates that the code is self-dual and the Hamming weight of all vectors in the code are congruent to $0 \pmod{4}.$  The question has remained open over 40 years and is the first in  a series of open questions about the existence of $[24k,12k,4k+4]$ Type~II codes. A number of attempts have been made to solve this problem, many of which have led to restrictions about the automorphism group of such a code if it exists. We can refer the reader to such works as \cite{Bouyuklieva}, \cite{Boyuklieva-2}, \cite{Nebe}, \cite{OBrien}, \cite{Yankov} and the references therein. The latest works indicate that the automorphism group of a doubly-even $[72,36,16]$ code has order $5$ or divides $24$.
Recently in \cite{Kier}, Kiermaier showed that the Gray image of a self-dual $\ZZ_4$ code cannot have parameters $(72, 2^{36},16)$.

In this paper we shall build on this and show that the extremal doubly-even $[72,36,16]$ code is not the Gray image of any linear code over $\ZZ_4$, $\FF_2 + u \FF_2$ or $\FF_2+v\FF_2$. In particular, this will show that the automorphism group of this code cannot have a fixed point  free involution. Bouyuklieva, in \cite{Bouyuklieva} showed that the automorphism group of the putative $[72,36,16]$ code cannot contain an automorphism of order $2$ with a positive number of fixed points. Combining the two results, we conclude that the automorphism group of the $[72,36,16]$ code cannot contain an automorphism of order 2, hence eliminating all even orders, leaving only $1$, $3$ and $5$ as the possibilities for the order of the automorphism group of such a code.
There are four rings of order 4, namely $\ZZ_4$, $\FF_4$, $\FF_2 + u \FF_2$, $u^2=0$ and $\FF_2 +  v \FF_2,$ $v^2=v.$
We will focus on the three rings that are not a field.
Each of these rings has a Gray map as given in the following:
Denote the Gray map for $\ZZ_4$ by $\phi_4$.
For $\FF_2 + u \FF_2$, denote the map by $\phi_u$ and define it  as  $\phi_u(a+bu) = (b,a+b).  $
For $\FF_2+ v \FF_2$ denote the map  by $\phi_v$ and define it  as $\phi_v(a+bv) = (a,a+b).$
The image under any of these maps is known as the Gray image of the code.  The map $\phi_4$ is not linear but $\phi_u$ and $\phi_v$ are linear.
The Lee weight of an element is the Hamming weight of its image under the Gray map.

Then for a vector the Lee weight is the sum of the Lee weights of its components.  The Lee weight enumerator for a code of length $n$  is defined as $L_C(x,y) = \sum_{\vc \in C} x^{N - wt(\vc)} y^{wt(\vc)}$ where $N=2n$ and $wt(\vc)$ is the Lee weight of the vector $\vc.$ Notice that the Hamming weight enumerator of the Gray image is simply the Lee weight enumerator for the code.
The inner-product is defined as: $[\vv,\vw] = \sum v_i w_i.$
When we need to differentiate in which ring the inner-product is being calculated we shall use
A code $C$ is self-dual if $C=C^\perp$ and is self-orthogonal if $C \subseteq C^\perp.$
We define a formally self-dual code as a code $C$ such that $L_C(x,y) = L_{C^\perp}(x,y).$
It is said to be Type~I if it has only even weights with at least one vector of weight $2 \pmod{4}.$  The code is said to be Type~II if all weights in the code are congruent to $0 \pmod{4}.$
The Gray image of a formally self-dual code  over $\ZZ_4$, $\FF_2+ u \FF_2$ or $\FF_2 +v \FF_2$ is a binary formally self-dual code.
The Gray image of a Type~II formally self-dual code over $\FF_2 +u \FF_2 $ or $\FF_2+v\FF_2$ is a binary self-dual doubly-even code.
The result follows from the definition of Type~II and the fact that Lee weight enumerator is equal to the Hamming weight enumerator of its Gray image.

The image of a self-dual code over $\ZZ_4$ can be non-linear or linear, and if it is linear it can be either self-dual or not self-dual.  The image of a self-dual code over $\FF_2 +u \FF_2$ or $\FF_2 + v \FF_2$ is a linear self-dual code.     See \cite{f2uf2} and \cite{AK} for details.  For a description of self-dual codes over $\ZZ_4$ see \cite{CS} and \cite{Pless}.  The images of self-dual codes over $\ZZ_4$ are described in \cite{cristina}.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we will talk about the torsion codes over $\ZZ_4$ and $\FF_2+u\FF_2$ and study some of the properties. In Section 3, we will show that the $[72,36,16]$-extremal code cannot be the Gray image of a linear code over $\ZZ_4$ or $\FF_2+u\FF_2$. In Section 4, we will prove that it cannot be the image of a linear code over $\FF_2+v\FF_2$.
In this section we shall describe Torsion codes over $\ZZ_4$ and $\FF_2+u\FF_2$.

It follows immediately that $Tor_0(C) \subseteq Tor_1(C)$  and that $|C| = |Tor_0(C)| |Tor_1(C)|.$
For codes over $\ZZ_4$ and $\FF_2+u\FF_2$, $Tor_0(C) = Tor_1(C)^\perp$ if and only if $C$ is a self-dual code of length $n$.
The result for self-dual codes is well known for both rings, see \cite{Pless} and \cite{f2uf2}.
We shall show the other direction for $\ZZ_4$, the proof for $\FF_2+u\FF_2$ is the same replacing $u$ for $2$.
Now assume $Tor_0(C) = Tor_1(C)^\perp.$    This gives that $|Tor_0(C)| |Tor_1(C)| = 2^n.$ Hence $|C| = 2^n$ and so has the size of a self-dual code.
Let $\vv \in Tor_0(C)$ and $\vw \in Tor_1(C)$.  We have that $[\vv,\vw]_2=0$ since the codes are orthogonal.

If we have a formally self-dual code over $\FF_2+u\FF_2$ or $\ZZ_4$ it is necessary to have    $$|Tor_0(C)| |Tor_1(C)| = 2^n$$ but we need a vector $\vv \in Tor_0(C)$ and $\vw \in Tor_1(C)$ such that $[\vv,\vw]_2 \neq 0.$
We can now give a generalization of Lemma~{3.2} in \cite{Kier}.
Let $C$ be a self-dual code over $\FF_2 + u \FF_2$  of even length   $n$ and minimum Lee distance $d$.

Then there exists a binary self-dual $[n,\frac{n}{2}]$ code $D$ such that the minimum distance of $D_0$ is at least $\frac{d}{2}$, where $D_0$ is the dual of the subcode of doubly-even vectors of $D$.

The proof follows as in \cite{Kier}.  Specifically, we have $Tor_0(C)$ is a self-orthogonal binary code. It is well known that there is a binary self-dual code $D$ containing $Tor_0(C)$.  We know $Tor_0(C)$ is doubly-even, and it is contained in $D_0$, so $(D_0^\perp) \subseteq (Tor_0(C))^\perp.$

But $(Tor_0(C))^\perp = Tor_1(C)$, and the minimum Hamming weight of $Tor_0(C) $ is less than or equal to the minimum Lee weight of $C$, which is less than or equal to $2 d_H(Tor_1(C)).$ This gives the result.
It is well known that in a binary linear code where all weights are doubly-even, the code must be self-orthogonal.
This follows from the fact that if the sum of two doubly-even vectors is doubly-even they must be orthogonal.

Over $\FF_2 + u \FF_2$  and $\ZZ_4$ this is not true.  For example, consider the vectors $(1+u,1+u,1+u,1+u,0,0,0,0)$ and $(1,1,1,0, 1,1,1,u)$. The first vector has weight 4 and the second has weight 8, their sum is
$(u,u,u,1+u,1,1,1,u)$ which has weight 12.  However, the inner-product of the two vectors is $1+u \neq 0.$

In \cite{f2uf2}, it is stated that $C$ is self-dual if and only if $\phi_u(C)$ is self-dual.  The proof, however, needs to be corrected, since it states that if the image of two vectors are orthogonal their their preimages are as well.  However, consider $(1)$ and $(1+u)$, their images are orthogonal but the vectors are not.  We now state a correct proof of this result.
Let $C$ be a code over $\FF_2+ u\FF_2$.  Then $C$ is self-dual if and only if $\phi_u(C)$ is a binary self-dual code.
It follows easily from the linearity of $\phi_u$ that if $C$ is self-dual then $\phi_u(C)$ is self-dual, see \cite{f2uf2}.
Next we handle the other direction.  Assume that $\phi_u(C)$ is a binary self-dual code.
Let $\vc_1,\vc_2 \in C$, with $\vc_1 = \vx_1 + u\vy_1$, $\vc_2 = \vx_2 + u\vy_2$, where $\vx_i,\vy_i$ are binary vectors.

The vectors $\vc_1 + \vc_2 = (\vx_1 + \vx_2)  + u (\vy_1 + \vy_2)$ and $u \vc_1 = \vx_1 u$ are both elements of $C$ since it is linear.
Then since $[\vx_1,\vx_1]_2 =0$ we have that $[\vx_1,\vx_2]_2=0$ and we have the result.
If $C$ is a Type~II formally self-dual code over $\FF_2+\FF_2$ then $C$ is self-dual.

If $C$ is a Type~II formally self-dual code over $\FF_2+\FF_2$ then by Theorem~\ref{images} we have that $\phi_u(C)$ is a Type~II binary formally self-dual code.  However, any doubly-even linear binary code must be self-orthogonal, hence it is self-dual since it has the proper cardinality.  Therefore, by Theorem~\ref{first}, the code $C$ must be self-dual.

The full result of Theorem~\ref{first} is not true for codes over $\ZZ_4$.  That is if $C$ is a self-dual code over $\ZZ_4$ its image may not be self-dual, in fact, it may not even be linear.  However, we can say the following.
Let $C$ be a code over $\ZZ_4$. If $\phi_4(C)$ is a binary self-dual code then $C$ is a quaternary self-dual code.

The proof follows similarly to the proof of Theorem~\ref{first}.  We begin by noticing that the every vector $\vc$ over $\ZZ_4$ can be viewed as $\vx + 2\vy$, with the Gray map defined as $\phi_4(\vc) = (\vy, \vx+\vy).$
Then replace $u$ with $2$ and the proof follows exactly.
In \cite{Kier}, Kiermaier proved that the image of a self-dual code over $\ZZ_4$ cannot have parameters $(72,2^{36},16)$.
This proof can be modified to prove the following.
If $C$ is a self-dual code over $\FF_2+u\FF_2$  then $\phi_u(C)$ is not a $[72,36,16]$ self-dual code.

The proof follows exactly as the proof in the $\ZZ_4$ case since we have the same results as given in the Torsion section.  Specifically, let $\phi_u(C)$ be a putative $[72,36,16]$ Type~II code. Then $C$ has length 36 and by Lemma~\ref{like32}, there exists a self-dual binary code $D$, with $D_0$ the subcode of doubly-even vectors, such that $D_0^\perp$ has minimum weight at least 8. But $D \subseteq D_0^\perp$ and $D$ can have minimum weight at most 8 by the standard bound from invariant theory, i.e.
This gives that the minimum weight of $D$ is 8.
The $[36,18,8]$ codes have been classified in \cite{Melchor}. Kiermaier checks in \cite{Kier}, that none of these has the correct weight for $D_0^\perp.$
\begin{thm} \label{big} A putative binary $[72,36,16]$ code is not the image of a linear code over $\FF_2+u \FF_2$ or $\ZZ_4$.

Let $C$ be a code over $\ZZ_4$ or $\FF_2 + u \FF_2$ whose image under the respective Gray map is the putative $[72,36,16]$ binary self-dual code.  Then the code $C$ must be a formally self-dual code since the Lee weight enumerator is the Hamming weight enumerator of a self-dual code and hence invariant under the MacWilliams relations.

Then by Theorem~\ref{first} and Theorem~\ref{second} the code $C$ must be a self-dual code.  Then Theorem~{1.1} in \cite{Kier} and Theorem~\ref{fourth} gives a contradiction since no self-dual code has as its image the specified binary code.
A putative self-dual $[72,36,16]$ Type~II code cannot have a fixed point free involution.
If the code had a fixed point free involution it would be the image of a linear $\FF_2 + u \FF_2$ code, which contradicts Theorem~\ref{big}.
Combining this with the result in \cite{Bouyuklieva} and the latest update in \cite{Nebe} we obtain the following important corollary:

The automorphism group of the doubly-even binary $[72,36,16]$ code cannot be of even order, hence it can only have order $1$, $3$ or $5$. In other words the automorphism group of the putative $[72,36,16]$ code is trivial,  $C_3$ or $C_5$.
Theorem \ref{big} answers one of the open problems posed in \cite{f2uf2}, namely we now can say that the minimum distance of a self-dual code over $\FF_2+u\FF_2$ of length $36$ can be at most $12$.
Theorem \ref{big}, combined with \cite{selfdualRk} implies that the $[72,36,16]$-code cannot be the image of a linear code over $R_k$.
In \cite{AK}, it is shown that $C$ is a self-dual code over $\FF_2+v\FF_2$ if and only if $C = CRT(C_1,C_2)$ where
$C_1$ and $C_2$ are binary self-dual codes, where $CRT$ is the map induced by the Chinese Remainder Theorem.
Let $C$ be a code over $\FF_2 + v \FF_2$.  The code $C$ is self-dual if and only if $\phi(C)$ is a binary self-dual code.
The fact that if $C$ is self-dual then $\phi(C)$ is self-dual follows easily from the fact that $\phi_v$ is linear, see \cite{AK} for details.

Assume $\phi_v(C)$ is self-dual. Then $C$ must at least be formally self-dual since its image has the weight enumerator of a self-dual code.  So we need to show that the code is self-orthogonal and it implies that it is a self-dual code.  Let $\vc_1, \vc_2 \in C.$  We need to show that $[\vc_1,\vc_2]_v=0.  $
We can write  $\vc_1 = \vx_1 + v\vy_1$, $\vc_2 = \vx_2 + v\vy_2$, where $\vx_i,\vy_i$ are binary vectors.
Then, we have that the image is permutation equivalent to the vectors $(\vx_1,\vx_1+\vy_1)$  and
$(\vx_2,\vx_2+\vy_2)$.  So we will simply say that  $\phi_v(\vc_1) = (\vx_1,\vx_1+\vy_1)$  and
Then we have that $[\phi_v(\vc_1),\phi_v(\vc_2)]_2 = 0$ which implies that
If we show that $ [\vx_1,\vx_2]_2 =0$ this implies that $ [\vx_1,\vy_2]_2  + [\vx_2,\vy_1]_2 +  [\vy_1,\vy_2]_2=0$ and we have that
We know that $v \vc_1$ and $v \vc_2$ are both in $C$, since $C$ is linear.  Then
Then by using Equation~\ref{eq2v} we have that $[\vx_1,\vx_2]_2=0$ and we have the result.
There does not exist a linear code over $\FF_2 + v\FF_2$ whose image is a $[72,36,16]$ Type~II code.

If $C$ is a code over $\FF_2 + v\FF_2$ whose image is a $[72,36,16]$ Type~II code, then $C$ must be a  self-dual code.  If $C$ is a self-dual code over $\FF_2+v\FF_2$ then $C=CRT(C_1,C_2)$, where $C_1,C_2$ are binary self-dual codes,  with minimum weight at least 16 and length 36.  However, it is shown in \cite{shadow} there are no length  36 binary self-dual codes with minimum distance 16.  Hence there is no linear code over $\FF_2 + v\FF_2$ whose image is a $[72,36,16]$ Type~II code.
